_comment: Phase 3 deletion ratchet (#1595 epic-0 unit 5). Each entry records ONE *_PATTERNS list actually deleted from services/intent_service/pre_classifier.py, with the evidence that licensed the deletion at the time. Non-regression (tests/unit/test_inversion_phase3_deletion_1595.py) re-checks EVERY entry on every run: none of its rows_claimed_at_deletion phrases may be claimed by any surviving surface-1 list, and each must still be a corpus row scoring MATCH or an agreeing REVIEW in the named report(s).

set a reminder for the dentist appointment
create a reminder to call the plumber
don't let me forget to submit the report
I need to remember to submit my timesheet
DELETED_PATTERN_LISTS.note: gate --list REMINDER_PATTERNS: GO, 5/5 literals exercised, 0 needs-a-corpus-row. 1 pre-existing REVIEW-agrees row ('remind me to review the roadmap tomorrow', router=create_reminder@1.0 vs claim=create_reminder, full-report) + 4 deposited rows scoring MATCH in the 2026-09-27 deposits report. Ceiling contribution: 567 -> 562 (this list alone).

gate --list REMINDER_QUERY_PATTERNS: GO, 4/4 literals exercised, 0 needs-a-corpus-row. 1 pre-existing REVIEW-agrees row ('what reminders do I have?', router=list_reminders_query@1.0 vs claim=list_reminders_query, full-report -- Arch's demanded Exhibit-A row) + 3 deposited rows scoring MATCH in the 2026-09-27 deposits report. Ceiling contribution: 567 -> 563 (this list alone); combined with REMINDER_PATTERNS in the same commit: 567 -> 558.

rows_claimed_at_deletion: what do I have next to do

what should I do next.note: PRIORITY_PATTERNS already carried an IDENTICAL literal (r"\bwhat should i do next\b") before this deletion -- verified via git blame: commit 33f3a43ad42, 2026-03-22, six months before TODO_QUERY_PATTERNS was touched. TODO_QUERY_PATTERNS's earlier position in pre_classify's if-chain shadowed it (first-claim-wins), so this literal was DEAD CODE for this exact phrase until TODO_QUERY_PATTERNS emptied. This is a genuine sibling-reabsorption finding (post-deletion census: corpus claimed dropped 110->100, not 110->101 -- 10 of the 11 rows genuinely unclaimed, this one reclaimed) -- named, not hidden, per the #1595 Phase 3 deletion procedure's own requirement. It is a DOCUMENTED, VERIFIED-AGREEING exception (not a silent drift): PRIORITY_PATTERNS's claim for this phrase is get_top_priority, byte-identical to the entry's own ruled expected_op_by_phrase destination and to the router's MATCH verdict in the todo-query-rescore report -- CXO/PPM's ruling and this pre-existing pattern independently arrived at the same answer. check_deleted_entry_non_regression treats this phrase as OK iff the reclaiming list still equals PRIORITY_PATTERNS AND its claimed action still agrees with expected_op_by_phrase -- any OTHER reclaim (different list, or an agreeing list whose answer later drifts) still fails loud, unchanged from every other phrase in this ledger.

DELETED_PATTERN_LISTS.note: gate --list TODO_QUERY_PATTERNS: GO, 10/10 literals exercised, 11/11 claimed rows, 0 needs-a-corpus-row. 3 pre-existing REVIEW-agrees rows ('show me my todos'/'show all my todos'/"what's my next todo?", each router=list_todos_query@1.0 vs their surface-1 claim -- full report) + 7 deposited rows scoring MATCH in the 2026-09-27 deposits report (expected action:list_todos_query) + 1 deposited row ('what should I do next') re-expected to action:get_top_priority and re-scored 1/1 MATCH by CXO/PPM ruling in the same-day todo-query-rescore report -- the original deposit expectation (list_todos_query) was a genuine MISMATCH against the router's get_top_priority answer, resolved by re-expecting the row rather than by forcing a wrong destination. expected_op_by_phrase records, PER PHRASE, which of the entry's two expected_ops each row actually verified against -- check_deleted_entry_non_regression and the reachability ratchet's phase3-deletion-ledger resolver both consult it in preference to the entry-wide 'any of expected_ops' fallback (that fallback stays correct for the other two single-op entries above; a heterogeneous-destination list needs the per-row answer, not 'any of them'). known_reabsorptions documents ONE post-deletion finding: 'what should I do next' is reclaimed by PRIORITY_PATTERNS (a pre-existing, previously-shadowed duplicate literal, not a new pattern) -- see that field for the full account. Ceiling contribution: 558 -> 548 (this list alone). | 2026-10-01: verdict of record moved to the served model (Haiku); 'what do I have next to do' routes get_top_priority there (decide-for-me 'next', CXO 09-27 shape) — row and this map updated, flagged to CXO.

shadowed_literals.\\bwhat'?s on my calendar.*tomorrow\\b: shadowed by \bwhat'?s on my calendar\b (earlier in the list; that pattern has no \b anchor requiring absence of trailing text, so it matches the 'tomorrow' phrasing too) -- never exercised.
shadowed_literals.\\bmy calendar tomorrow\\b: shadowed by \bcalendar.*tomorrow\b (earlier in the list, strictly broader) -- never exercised.

DELETED_PATTERN_LISTS.note: gate --list CALENDAR_QUERY_PATTERNS --live read_status,read_referent,read_synthesis,create_todo,create_reminder,read_strategic,read_temporal: GO, 49/49 claimed rows MATCH/agreeing-REVIEW/live-MISMATCH, 0 needs-a-corpus-row (3 literals structurally shadowed -- see shadowed_literals, not a blocker). Verdict of record: the served-model (Haiku) baseline + the CALENDAR-specific rescores + CXO's 10-01 ruling on the 5 capability-gap rows (no-feature asks honestly floor rather than claim a week dump as an answer). 19 of the 49 phrases are REABSORBED by TEMPORAL_PATTERNS post-deletion (disagreeing -- claimed as get_current_time, never agreeing with the ruled meeting_time/week_calendar/recurring_meetings/floor destination) -- a sibling-takeover finding an order of magnitude larger than the second deletion's single PRIORITY_PATTERNS case, reported in full under known_reabsorptions (each entry's agrees=false), never silenced. check_deleted_entry_non_regression and expected_op_for_phrase were extended (same commit) to accept a documented DISAGREEING reclaim when the phrase's own frozen router evidence independently re-proves it safe (the SAME MATCH/agreeing-REVIEW/live-MISMATCH proof build_census used at gate time, re-derived via row_disposition with a synthetic claim carrying the phrase's resolved target op) -- sound because production's consult_inversion_live runs BEFORE this surface-1 fallback and already proves the row safe; the TEMPORAL reclaim only bites when the live consult stands down. This is a NEW general capability (cats threading + the unified row_disposition re-derivation covers BOTH the reclaimed and the unclaimed-but-MISMATCH-live case), not CALENDAR-specific -- check_deleted_entry_non_regression's non-regression re-check now requires the SAME --live categories (read_temporal) the original gate run used; omitted/None cats (the strictest reading) reproduces the pre-this-commit behavior byte for byte for every earlier ledger entry, none of which ever needed a live condition. Ceiling: 548 -> 496 (this list alone).
